purpose: verify that the pinned public NASICON inputs and a controlled wrapper execute end to end on the configured SSH platform
interpretation: implementation smoke test only; no scientific comparison or convergence claim

arms.pairing: reset the same Python and NumPy random seed before each structure

required_outputs: initial and final active-event barrier/rate summaries
initial and final active-event graph component summaries
runtime, event count, package versions, and pass/fail gate
success_rule: both structures complete with finite positive simulated time, finite final transport metrics, exactly three measurement summaries, nonempty active-event graphs, and the expected upstream commit
nonclaims: three measurement passes are not converged long-time transport
the smoke-test conductivity is not comparable to experiment
connected components of the instantaneous active-event graph do not establish periodic percolation
successful execution does not validate the fitted physical model
